content: The designations and presentation of material in this publication do not imply any opinion from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) or the World Health Organization (WHO) regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, or its authorities, nor do they imply any judgment on the delimitation of its frontiers or boundaries. Dotted lines on maps represent approximate borderlines for which there may not yet be full agreement. The mention of specific companies or products, whether patented or not, does not imply endorsement or recommendation by FAO or WHO over others of a similar nature that are not mentioned. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters, except for errors or omissions. FAO and WHO have taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information contained in this publication. However, the material is distributed without any warranty, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for the interpretation and use of the material lies with the reader. FAO and WHO shall not be liable for any damages arising from its use. The views expressed in this publication are those of the authors and do not necessarily represent those of FAO or WHO. FAO and WHO encourage the use, reproduction, and dissemination of material in this information product. However, compliance with FAO and WHO specifications does not constitute an endorsement or warranty of the fitness of a particular pesticide for a specific purpose, including its suitability for controlling a given pest or its appropriateness for use in a particular area. The suitability of pesticides for a specific purpose and the content of labeling instructions must be determined at the national or provincial level. Pesticides manufactured to comply with these specifications are not exempt from any safety regulations or other legal or administrative provisions applicable to their manufacture, sale, transportation, storage, handling, preparation, and/or use. FAO and WHO disclaim any liability for injury, death, loss, damage, or other prejudice of any kind that may arise as a result of, or in connection with, the manufacture, sale, transportation, storage, handling, preparation, and/or use of pesticides claimed to comply with these specifications. Improper storage, handling, preparation, and/or use of pesticides can result in a reduction or complete loss of safety and/or efficacy. FAO and WHO are not responsible for testing pesticides for compliance with the specifications, nor for any methods recommended or used for testing compliance. Consequently, FAO and WHO do not warrant or represent that any pesticide claimed to comply with a FAO or WHO specification actually does so. Confidential proprietary data or information provided for evaluation by the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Specifications (JMPS) will be safeguarded from unauthorized release or disclosure. Experts participating in the JMPS are required to sign confidentiality agreements and restrictions on use. They are also required to declare any actual or potential conflicts of interest and will not participate in discussions where such conflicts arise, except to provide information if required. Following the completion of evaluations and specifications, all data, including proprietary data, will be returned to FAO or WHO and kept secure. If a specification is withdrawn, FAO or WHO will contact the proposer to determine whether the data package should be destroyed or returned. Confidential data and information do not become the property of FAO or WHO. FAO specifications for pesticides were developed to promote the manufacture, distribution, and use of pesticides that meet basic quality requirements. These specifications are published on the internet and are integral with the corresponding evaluations of data, allowing users to understand the scientific reasoning behind the specifications. The WHO Pesticide Evaluation Scheme (WHOPES) was established in 1960 to promote and coordinate the testing and evaluation of pesticides intended for public health use. WHOPES operates within the framework of the International Code of Conduct on the Distribution and Use of Pesticides, promoting the safe handling, efficacy, cost-effective application, and quality control of pesticide products and formulations for public health use. WHOPES collaborates with national disease and pest control programs, pesticide registration authorities, international organizations, research institutions, and industry. Its recommendations are based on published and unpublished data and consider factors influencing product performance for specific applications. Local testing is necessary to determine performance under specific conditions and target species.
